subject: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@optimumai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@optimumai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API

Hi Ben —

We’re reviewing our monthly budget guardrails and want to understand how Redwood handles cases when we exceed our anticipated spend on the hosted API. A couple of things procurement wants clarified:

- Can you enforce a hard spend cap so API calls stop once we hit a threshold?
- Is there a soft-cap flow with automated warnings (email/webhook) before anything is blocked?
- Do you offer pre-authorized overage charges (card on file) vs. manual approval for charges beyond the committed amount?
- If traffic spikes, is there an option for temporary throttling or per-route rate limiting rather than full stop?

We’re evaluating three outcomes for purchase order language: (1) hard cap, no exceptions, (2) soft-cap with automatic 24–48hr grace and card charge, (3) auto-scale but with daily notifications and monthly true-up. Please point me to any standard wording, policy docs, and how these are implemented in the product/API.

Also, procurement will need a short SOW/attachment showing billing terms if we move forward.

Thanks —
Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Platform Ops, OptimumAI
Procurement: procurement@optimumai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@optimumai.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is how Redwood typically handles spend thresholds and the options we support. I’ll also attach our standard overage policy and a draft SOW for OptimumAI so procurement has something to circulate.

Options we offer (summary):

1) Hard cap (block):
- We can configure an account-level hard cap. Once reached, the serving runtime rejects further generation calls (429 / 402 depending on your preference) until the cap is increased.
- Pros: predictable spend, zero surprise charges.
- Cons: possible user-facing errors if you get a sudden spike.

2) Soft cap (alerts + grace window):
- Soft threshold triggers automated notifications (email + webhook). You can set a 24–72 hour grace period where traffic is allowed but flagged. After the window, calls are either blocked or routed to a lower-cost variant.
- We provide webhook events for threshold_crossed, threshold_warning, and threshold_reset.

3) Auto-approve overage (pre-authorized payment):
- If you provide a card on file (or establish a billing mandate), we can allow automatic billing for overages up to a negotiated limit, with a daily cap to limit runaways.
- We can couple this with daily spend reports and per-route caps.

Additional product levers: throttling by route, per-model token caps, prefix/KV cache enforcement to reduce token spend, and automatic fallback to quantized or smaller models if cost exceeds a policy.

Business-side controls:
- We can add a clause in the SOW: preferred default is soft-cap + 24hr grace for production rollouts, with an option to opt into hard-cap for sensitive environments.
- For enterprise commits we typically allow a negotiated overage policy: e.g., first month overage credited 10% (one-time) if you sign an annual commitment within 30 days.

Attachments: Redwood-Overage-Policy-v1.pdf (policy), SOW-Draft-Optimum-8742.pdf (draft).

Next steps:
- If procurement prefers the hard cap, we’ll need to coordinate with finance/legal for wording and confirm whether you want a 402 (payment required) vs. 429 (rate limited) response surface.
- If you want soft-cap + webhook, I can share the webhook schema and a short runbook.

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the trade-offs?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Sam Turner <sam.turner@optimumai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API

Ben / Sam —

Quick operational notes from infra/product:
- We strongly recommend the webhook-based alerting as the first line; it’s low friction and lets customers instrument an automated pause if desired.
- Card-on-file auto-approve should have a daily monetary ceiling (we typically suggest 10–20% of committed monthly spend) to prevent runaway charges.
- For customers who want a hard cap, we can map that to a tenant flag in the control plane and expose an API to increase the cap; changes require an authorized role.

Happy to hop on the technical portion of the call.

—Connor
Director, Platform Reliability
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@optimumai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@optimumai.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API

Thanks Ben and Connor — helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement: we need explicit language about refunds/credits if an overage is caused by platform issues (e.g., mis-routing, billing bug). Also: can the soft-cap flow be limited to specific API routes (ingestion vs. generation) so we don’t block telemetry calls?

Procurement also requested a clean PDF of the billing terms for the PO (tax info, billing cadence, and remit instructions).

If you can confirm the refund policy and route-level soft-cap before our PO submission, that will speed things up.

Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@optimumai.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing thresholds & enforcement options for hosted API

Sam —

Short answers: yes on both.

- Refunds/credits: If an overage is demonstrably due to Redwood platform behavior (routing bug, billing pipeline error, etc.), we will issue a pro-rata credit for the impacted period after an investigation. We’ll include a standard redress clause in the SOW.
- Route-scoped soft-cap: supported. You can define threshold rules at the route/model/tenant level so ingestion or telemetry routes can be excluded from blocking flows.

I’ve added a link to a DocuSign powerform for the SOW template in the related links above, and attached the SOW draft with billing and tax sections filled in for OptimumAI.

As a gesture to expedite the procurement decision, Marissa has okayed a one-time 10% courtesy credit on the first month’s overage if OptimumAI signs an annual committed plan within 30 days. This will be reflected in the SOW if you confirm.

Would you like me to update the SOW and send a final for signature?

Best,
Ben
